title: terraform: private - restructure GPU node pool modules, IAM roles, networking and remote state layout
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Refactors Terraform modules for Private deployments: GPU node pools, IAM roles, VPC networking, and remote state layout. Improves upgrade paths and reduces drift risk.
body:
Motivation: Private deploy customers (VPC/on-prem installer) reported drift and brittle upgrade behavior for GPU node pool composition and for IAM policies that vary by cloud provider. This PR standardizes the module boundaries, moves provider-agnostic pieces into `modules/common`, and lays out a stable remote state architecture to make incremental upgrades and rollbacks safer.

What it does: 1) Adds `modules/gpu-node-pool` (provider-abstracted) with a concrete GKE/AKS/EC2 submodule mapping; 2) Reworks `modules/iam` into small role attachments + mappings to reduce diff size when adding policies; 3) Reconciles networking patterns into `modules/networking` and extracts shared subnets and route tables; 4) Introduces `state/backend.tf` and migration helpers to move from a flat state to per-environment/state-per-module layout to reduce lock contention and allow targeted applies.

Key changes: - New module: modules/gpu-node-pool (encapsulates autoscaling, taints, gpu-accelerator configs) - IAM: split role definitions vs attachments; added least-privilege templates for node pools - Networking: explicit shared VPC module, optional subnet isolation for private clusters - State: backend refactor + migration plan (see NOTES_ON_UPGRADE below)

Checklist: [x] terraform fmt & validate; [x] unit module tests; [x] staged plan in CI; [x] canary apply in test VPC; [x] docs and examples updated - https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-4021

Notes: Description and migration steps below include commands and examples. This PR intentionally avoids provider-specific breaking changes; provider-specific adapters are implemented as separate submodules so consumers can opt-in when moving to the new layout.

References: Linear ENG-4021, infra notes in SUP-789, previous PRs pr-18345 and pr-20455 for state layout discussion.
commits: a1f3d2c: feat(modules): add modules/gpu-node-pool with provider-abstracted interface
b4e7f90: refactor(iam): split roles and attachments; add least-privilege templates
c3d9b11: feat(networking): extract shared_vpc and subnet isolation options
d2a8e66: ops(state): introduce backend.tf layout and migration helper script
e5f1c22: docs: update examples/private and README with migration guide
review_comments: Lucas Rivera: Can we avoid forcing a state migration for customers who are still on the old layout? Suggest adding opt-in migration plan and retain backward compatibility.
Maya Chen: Added an opt-in migration helper script (scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh) and documented the step-by-step process. Default remains the old layout unless user runs the migrate script.
Ethan Cole: IAM split looks good; please add explicit tests that role attachments are idempotent across repeated applies.
Maya Chen: Added unit tests and an integration check in CI that runs two consecutive applies against the module (see pipeline step integration-tests:gpu-node-pool).
Priya Nair: Minor: update the examples/README to show how to pin the provider adapters when rolling forward.
notes_on_upgrade: BACKUP: Always backup the existing state before running migration: terraform state pull > state-backup-<env>.tfstate
MIGRATE SCRIPT: ./scripts/tfstate-migrate.sh --from flat --to per-module --env=staging will create targeted state files and update the backend configuration. Run in CI with proper credentials first.
ROLLBACK: If migration fails, reupload the backed-up state with terraform state push state-backup-<env>.tfstate and revert to previous commit.
ROLLING UPGRADE: Use per-module apply order: networking -> iam -> gpu-node-pool -> cluster to avoid transient IAM/network race conditions.
KUBE: For GKE/AKS upgrades that change node pool identifiers, we rely on node labels/taints to safely cordon/drain; see examples/private/gke-gpu/cluster.tf for pattern.
test_summary: Canary apply in staging VPC with 1 GPU node pool - validated autoscaler behavior and taint propagation
Integration: double-apply idempotency tests for IAM role attachments passed
E2E: basic node lifecycle (create, cordon, drain, delete) exercised against GKE adapter
Smoke: example stacks in examples/private built and deployed successfully
suggested_followups: ENG-4022: Add AKS/EC2 adapter tests and provider matrix in CI
INFRA-222: Add monitoring dashboards for per-module state lock contention
Docs: walkthrough for enterprise customers to automate the migration via runbooks and IAM break-glass steps
